title: Do Open Replication Circuit Tracers Reproduce the Planning-Ahead Result?

original_idea.body:
# Do Open Replication Circuit Tracers Reproduce the Planning-Ahead Result?

**Problem:** Anthropic reported Claude 3.5 Haiku plans rhyming words ahead, shown only on a proprietary model. Unknown whether the same planning circuit appears in small open models.

**Direction:** Using the open Circuit Tracer library, build attribution graphs to test forward-planning of rhyme words across three open model families.

**Why it matters:** Forward-planning latents are alignment-relevant; confirming in open models tells us if it's studiable outside labs.

**Relevant context:** transformer-circuits.pub 2025; Circuit Tracer; EleutherAI Attribute.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (planning is alignment-relevant) but replicating a poetry-planning result has a gappy link to catastrophic risk.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Uses released Circuit Tracer on supported open models; inherited methodology, guided.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused replication across three models with a clear question, few dependencies.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open tooling/models, replication labs won't redo; independent-friendly.

low_compute.reasoning: Attribution graphs on small open models; single mid GPU.

novelty.reasoning: The proprietary result is published; open-model replication is plausibly not yet done.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: The original result is published; open-model replication may be open.
